scenario.name: Baseline

notes: O-D travel time +0.0% over 114 gateway pairs

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).
baseline.summary: Baseline: no failures applied. All modelled systems operate normally — 134.1 MW of load served, 435.0 L/s of water demand met, 16 telecom endpoints connected and 20 transport destinations accessible.

presets.name: DS Five Points substation failure
presets.description: DS-2 Five Points (simulated) trips. Its three radial feeders lose supply; normally-open ties to Centennial, Capitol and Peachtree Center can only pick up part of the load, and the outage cascades into water pumping, telecom, signals and MARTA.

scenario.name: DS Five Points substation failure

presets.name: Excavation strike on Edgewood Ave duct bank (Grady / Georgia State)
presets.description: A contractor strikes the shared Edgewood Ave duct bank between Courtland St and Jesse Hill Jr Dr. Every cable in the trench is cut at once: feeder GR-1 (one of Grady's two power feeds, plus the traction feed for Georgia State station) and the fibre backhaul of BOTH access nodes that give Grady its 'diverse' communications paths (common-cause failure).

scenario.name: Excavation strike on Edgewood Ave duct bank (Grady / Georgia State)

presets.name: Transmission main break on Decatur St
presets.description: A transmission water main ruptures on Decatur St east of Five Points; crews must close isolation valves, cutting supply to part of the low-pressure grid.

scenario.name: Transmission main break on Decatur St

presets.name: 56 Marietta St carrier hotel outage
presets.description: The core interconnection facility at 56 Marietta St (real building; modelled connections simulated) goes dark. The dual-homed fibre rings fail over to the east core, but the Capitol Hill access node and the Five Points rooftop cell are backhauled only into 56 Marietta: City Hall and the Fulton County Courthouse lose communications.

scenario.name: 56 Marietta St carrier hotel outage

presets.name: Five Points cordon (road closures)
presets.description: An emergency cordon closes the Five Points intersection, the Marietta St / Broad St corner outside Five Points station and the adjoining blocks of Peachtree St, Marietta St and Edgewood Ave. Traffic detours around the core and Five Points station loses its street access.

scenario.name: Five Points cordon (road closures)

presets.name: Loss of TS-South bulk supply (overload cascade)
presets.description: The TS-South 115 kV bulk supply point (simulated) is lost. DS-2 Five Points shifts onto its alternate line from TS-West, which was never rated for the full load: it runs above its 120% emergency limit, trips in the next round, and Five Points blacks out - a true overload cascade.

scenario.name: Loss of TS-South bulk supply (overload cascade)

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).
A-DS-FIVEPOINTS.summary: DS Five Points substation failure: failure of PWR-DS-FIVEPOINTS (DS-2 Five Points (simulated)) affects 39 nodes across 5 systems (facility, power, telecom, transport, water) over 2 cascade steps; severity index 30.5/100. Power: 21.1 of 134.1 MW unserved, 10.4 MW restored through 3 tie switches, Feeder CEN-2 section 1 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117%, Feeder CEN-2 section 2 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117% and 4 more (overloaded but below the 120% trip limit). Water: 0.0 L/s of demand unserved (3 zones carried by storage tanks). Telecom: 1 node without connectivity. Transport: O-D travel time +4.6%, 2 transit stations closed, 2 delayed by more than 25%, 7 destinations reached by detour. Critical facilities affected: Atlanta Police Department Headquarters (on backup), Atlanta City Hall (on backup) and Fulton County Courthouse (on backup). Estimated population affected: 19,620. Redundancy (meshing, tie switching, rerouting, storage, detours) recovered 59% of the service initially cut.

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).
F-TS-SOUTH.summary: Loss of TS-South bulk supply (overload cascade): failure of PWR-TS-SOUTH (TS-South 115 kV bulk supply (simulated)) affects 40 nodes across 5 systems (facility, power, telecom, transport, water) over 3 cascade steps; severity index 30.5/100. Power: 21.1 of 134.1 MW unserved, 10.4 MW restored through 3 tie switches, Feeder CEN-2 section 1 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117%, Feeder CEN-2 section 2 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117% and 4 more (overloaded but below the 120% trip limit), TL-02 TS-West 115 kV bulk supply → DS-2 Five Points (115 kV, simulated) tripped on overload. Water: 0.0 L/s of demand unserved (3 zones carried by storage tanks). Telecom: 1 node without connectivity. Transport: O-D travel time +4.6%, 2 transit stations closed, 2 delayed by more than 25%, 7 destinations reached by detour. Critical facilities affected: Atlanta Police Department Headquarters (on backup), Atlanta City Hall (on backup) and Fulton County Courthouse (on backup). Estimated population affected: 19,620. Redundancy (meshing, tie switching, rerouting, storage, detours) recovered 68% of the service initially cut.

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).
scenario_a.summary: DS Five Points substation failure: failure of PWR-DS-FIVEPOINTS (DS-2 Five Points (simulated)) affects 39 nodes across 5 systems (facility, power, telecom, transport, water) over 2 cascade steps; severity index 30.5/100. Power: 21.1 of 134.1 MW unserved, 10.4 MW restored through 3 tie switches, Feeder CEN-2 section 1 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117%, Feeder CEN-2 section 2 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 117% and 4 more (overloaded but below the 120% trip limit). Water: 0.0 L/s of demand unserved (3 zones carried by storage tanks). Telecom: 1 node without connectivity. Transport: O-D travel time +4.6%, 2 transit stations closed, 2 delayed by more than 25%, 7 destinations reached by detour. Critical facilities affected: Atlanta Police Department Headquarters (on backup), Atlanta City Hall (on backup) and Fulton County Courthouse (on backup). Estimated population affected: 19,620. Redundancy (meshing, tie switching, rerouting, storage, detours) recovered 59% of the service initially cut.

assumptions: Screening model, not a validated engineering model: results show plausible impact paths on a partly simulated/estimated network (see provenance), not certified outcomes.
Power: energisation by graph connectivity (BFS) from transmission substations over closed elements; no AC power flow, voltage, fault-current or protection-coordination study.
Power: loading = sum of served demand on the radial supply path (no losses, unity power factor); >100% of rating = overloaded, >120% emergency limit = protective trip in the next round.

Power: normally-open ties close automatically when the headroom — tie capacity, supplying substations' spare capacity (rating − served load) and the supplying cables'/lines' 120% emergency rating — covers the de-energised island; otherwise vaults are restored in priority order (critical consumers incl. pumps, telecom cores and hospitals, then larger loads) along the feeder and the rest is sectionalised off. Substation buses are not back-fed.

Power: a tie whose SCADA control link is down can only be closed manually after its manual_switch_hours (default 3 h) — only if that fits within the horizon; ties without a control link are assumed remote-controlled.
Water: hydraulics approximated by max-flow (no pressures or head losses); pressure zones modelled with a two-layer graph — high zones need an operating booster pump or elevated storage.

Water: a rupture closes the nearest isolation valves (BFS through non-valve nodes); stations and zone connections are assumed to have their own isolation valves; normally-closed boundary valves stay closed and are listed as alternatives.

Water: storage tanks only cover demand the supply network cannot meet; duration = storage / outflow; zones on a tank that lasts the horizon are on backup, otherwise in outage after depletion. Zone service ≥98% operational, ≥50% degraded (low pressure), <50% outage.

Telecom: connectivity = path over operational fibre to any operating internet exchange / data centre; shortest-path routing by latency/length; capacity check sums endpoint demand along routes (no protocol/QoS model).
Backup (backup_power_hours / backup_hours / water_storage_hours) counts only when it covers the horizon; missing backup properties mean no backup.

Transport: static shortest-path travel times (travel_time_s, else length / speed, default 40 km/h); dark signals add +25 s per approach; no congestion feedback. Destinations delayed above +25% travel time; road flows are an O-D assignment index (busiest baseline edge at 85% of capacity), not counted traffic.
Transit: stations close without station/traction power (no backup) or when severed from every other open station.
Underground: damage to a duct bank / utility tunnel segment or a utility vault fails every edge routed through it.

Dependencies: a consumer loses a resource only when all its providers lose service; losing some providers is reported as lost redundancy. One dependency hop per cascade round; losses are not reversed in later rounds.

Severity index = 100 × (0.20·√x_power + 0.15·√x_water + 0.15·√x_telecom + 0.15·√x_transport + 0.25·√x_facilities + 0.10·√x_population); x_power = unserved MW / baseline MW; x_water = unserved L/s / baseline L/s; x_telecom = (endpoints without service + 0.3 × congested) / endpoints; x_transport = min(1, Δ O-D travel time %/100 + share of O-D pairs unreachable + 0.5 × share of stations closed); x_facilities = Σ impact / critical facilities (outage/inaccessible 1, degraded 0.5 — 0.25 if only a redundant feed was lost — on backup/delayed 0.25); x_population = affected / modelled population; every x clipped to [0, 1].

Population affected = max(residents of de-energised vaults, water zones without full supply, disconnected telecom endpoints) + occupants of facilities in outage/inaccessible (max avoids double counting).
scenario_b.summary: Excavation strike on Edgewood Ave duct bank (Grady / Georgia State): failure of UGD-DB-06 (Edgewood Ave duct bank (Courtland St - Jesse Hill Jr Dr, Grady / Georgia State) (simulated)) affects 12 nodes across 4 systems (facility, power, telecom, transport) over 2 cascade steps; severity index 23.7/100. The failure is common-cause: 4 hosted edges (power, telecom) are routed through corridor UGD-DB-06 (Edgewood Ave duct bank (Courtland St - Jesse Hill Jr Dr, Grady / Georgia State) (simulated)). Power: 5.0 of 134.1 MW unserved, 2.4 MW restored through 1 tie switch, Feeder CAP-1 section 1 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 105% and Feeder CAP-1 section 2 (12.47 kV, simulated) loaded to 105% (overloaded but below the 120% trip limit). Telecom: 2 nodes without connectivity. Transport: O-D travel time +0.2%, 2 transit stations closed, 5 destinations reached by detour. Critical facilities affected: Grady Memorial Hospital (degraded). Estimated population affected: 5,020. Redundancy (meshing, tie switching, rerouting, storage, detours) recovered 10% of the service initially cut.

steps.title: Downtown Atlanta as one living system
steps.narration: This is downtown Atlanta — Five Points, Peachtree Center, the Capitol and Grady — rebuilt as a digital twin. Streets and landmarks are approximate; every utility asset beneath them is an illustrative simulation.

steps.title: Go beneath the street
steps.narration: Deep mode peels the city open. Pipes, cables, duct banks and rail tunnels are drawn at modelled depth, so you can see what normally only shows up when someone digs.

steps.title: Six interdependent networks
steps.narration: Power, water, internet, transportation, shared underground corridors and critical facilities. The thin links between them are dependencies: pumps need power, signals need power, switches need comms.

steps.title: DS-2 Five Points (simulated)
steps.narration: This simulated distribution substation feeds the heart of downtown through three radial feeders. Its inspector shows rating, load and provenance, labelled SIMULATED.

steps.title: Trace what depends on it
steps.narration: Tracing downstream lights up every vault, the booster pump, the 56 Marietta carrier hotel, City Hall, MARTA Five Points and dozens of traffic signals that hang off this one substation.

steps.title: Fail the substation
steps.narration: Scenario A trips DS Five Points. The engine finds every customer that lost its path to a source, then closes normally-open ties to pick up what it can.

steps.title: Watch the cascade
steps.narration: Round by round the failure spreads: feeders de-energise, signals go dark and traffic slows, the high-pressure water zone falls back on its tank, cell sites run down their batteries. Ties restore only part of the load — they were never sized for all of it.

steps.title: Ask the analyst
steps.narration: The AI analyst answers from the simulation results, not guesswork: it cites the elements that failed, why restoration was partial, and which upgrades would have helped most.
steps.question: Why did this happen, and what could we do differently?

steps.title: One shovel, four systems
steps.narration: Scenario B is a single excavation strike on the Edgewood Ave duct bank beside Grady. One feeder, its station traction feed and both of the hospital's 'diverse' fibre paths share that trench, so one cut hits power, telecom, transit and Grady at once.

steps.title: Compare A and B
steps.narration: Side by side: the substation loss drops far more load and puts City Hall on generators; the trench strike drops less load but cuts the hospital's communications and shuts the east-line MARTA stations. Shared corridors are the hidden single points of failure.

Why did this happen, and what could we d.text:
The cascade starts at DS-2 Five Points (simulated) (`PWR-DS-FIVEPOINTS`) and reaches 38 other component(s): 11 element(s) in the same network stay down because the alternative paths were capacity-limited; 27 component(s) in Critical facilities, Internet, Transportation, Water depend on it — 4 lose service, 8 run on backup for now.

**What the simulation shows**
- Severity index **30/100**; **39** components affected over **3** cascade steps (assessed 4 h after onset).
- Electricity: **21.1 MW** of load unserved.
- Internet: **1** endpoints disconnected from the core.
- Transport: average modelled travel time **+5%**.
- Transit: **2** rail station(s) closed.
- Critical facilities affected: Atlanta Police Department Headquarters (`FAC-APDHQ`, on backup), Atlanta City Hall (`FAC-CITYHALL`, on backup), Fulton County Courthouse (`FAC-COURTHOUSE`, on backup).

**Why it cascades**
- **Step 0**: Initiating failure: DS-2 Five Points (simulated)
- **Step 1**: Direct impact — Power: 11 nodes de-energised, 7 nodes restored by tie switching
- **Step 2**: Dependency: 22 consumers lose power → Water: Fairlie-Poplar booster pump station (simulated) without power (booster bypassed), 4 nodes on backup · Telecom: Cell site Five Points rooftop (simulated)…

**Consequences by system**
- Electricity: 11 element(s) remain de-energised, 7 restored by automatic tie switching (21.1 MW unserved).
- Critical facilities: on backup: Atlanta Police Department Headquarters, Atlanta City Hall, Fulton County Courthouse.
- Water: outage: Fairlie-Poplar booster pump station (simulated); on backup: North elevated storage tank (simulated), Civic Center service zone (high) (simulated), North Avenue service zone (high) (simulated) +1 more.
- Internet: outage: Cell site Five Points rooftop (simulated); on backup: 56 Marietta St carrier hotel.
- Transportation: closed: Five Points station (MARTA), Garnett station (MARTA); degraded: Peachtree St & John Wesley Dobbs Ave, Marietta St & Forsyth St, Peachtree St & Auburn Ave +12 more.

**What already helped**
- Tie PWR-SW-TIE01 (Tie switch 01 FP-1 ↔ CEN-2 (simulated)) closed (automatic) back-feeds PWR-NV-013 (Vault 013 Centennial Olympic Park Dr & Marietta St (simulated)) from PWR-DS-CENTENNIAL (DS-1… _(capacity-limited)_
- Tie PWR-SW-TIE02 (Tie switch 02 FP-2 ↔ CAP-1 (simulated)) closed (automatic) back-feeds PWR-NV-017 (Vault 017 Trinity Ave & Washington St (simulated)) from PWR-DS-CAPITOL (DS-3 Capitol (simulated)):… _(capacity-limited)_
- Tie PWR-SW-TIE03 (Tie switch 03 FP-3 ↔ PT-1 (simulated)) closed (automatic) back-feeds PWR-NV-021 (Vault 021 Peachtree St & Ellis St & Luckie St (simulated)) from PWR-DS-PEACHTREE (DS-4 Peachtree… _(capacity-limited)_

**What we could do differently**
- Add 8 h of backup power at Cell site Five Points rooftop (simulated) (`TEL-CELL-02`), which goes dark because its backup does not cover the 4 h horizon. **Modelled effect:** severity 30 → 27, affected components 39 → 39, telecom endpoints disconnected 1.0 → 0.0.
- Add 8 h of backup power at Five Points station (MARTA) (`TRN-STN-FIVEPOINTS`), which goes dark because its backup does not cover the 4 h horizon. **Modelled effect:** severity 30 → 28, affected components 39 → 38, transit stations closed 2.0 → 0.0.
- Reinforce the restoration path through tie `PWR-SW-TIE03` (double the rating of `PWR-TIE-03A`, `PWR-TIE-03B`, `PWR-FDR-0049`, `PWR-FDR-0048`, `PWR-FDR-0050`); automatic restoration was capacity-limited there. **Modelled effect:** severity 30 → 29, affected components 39 → 35, population affected (modelled) 19,620.0 → 14,480.0 people, power unserved 21.1 → 16.0 MW.
- Also tested, with no modelled improvement in this scenario: Reinforce the restoration path through tie `PWR-SW-TIE01`; Reinforce the restoration path through tie `PWR-SW-TIE02`.

**Data caveats** — Results come from DEEPTRACE's simplified deterministic model (no AC power flow, max-flow hydraulics surrogate), not a validated engineering prediction. Affected elements by provenance: 21 estimated, 18 simulated; simulated assets are illustrative, not real utility records.
